title: Predicting Spatial Gene Expression from Routine H&E Histology in Unseen Patients: A Leave-One-Patient-Out Evaluation in HER2-Positive Breast Cancer and Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma
content: Background/Objectives: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) is costly and rarely available in routine care, whereas hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) slides exist for almost every tumour. Many published estimates of expression predicted from H&E use evaluations in which the test patient's tissue was also seen in training. We asked how well expression can be predicted for unseen patients. Methods: We built REGEN, an ensemble of a frozen Phikon encoder and fine-tuned DenseNet121 and ResNet50 networks, with k-nearest-neighbour retrieval on the two CNN branches. We evaluated it by leave-one-patient-out validation on two public cohorts, Her2ST (HER2-positive breast cancer, 8 patients) and cSCC (cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, 4 patients), against a corrected reimplementation of a joint-contrastive model (MViTGene). Results: On the 50 most highly expressed genes (HEG), REGEN reached a mean Pearson correlation of 0.158 on Her2ST and 0.210 on cSCC, against 0.035 and 0.030 for the baseline. Over all 1,000 panel genes, correlations were much lower and concentrated in strongly expressed immune, stromal and epidermal genes. Choosing ensemble weights without the evaluated patient changed HEG by at most 0.005, whereas a gene panel selected on all sections differed in up to 37% of its genes without the held-out patient. On cSCC the correlation fell from 0.21 within patients to 0.05 after pooling patients. REGEN did not reach published mclSTExp values, whose protocol we could not verify. Conclusions: Predicted expression for unseen patients is modest and uneven across genes and patients, and does not support clinical use. With 8 and 4 patients the findings are exploratory; the contribution is a protocol-controlled comparison, not a new architecture.
